variants.title: Trace the request
variants.context: A request is a message asking a service to do work. The service interprets it and reads durable data when needed.
variants.prompt: A user opens a short link. Build the request path before a response can be sent.

items.text: The database returns the saved destination.
The browser sends a request.
The service asks the database for the saved destination.
The service receives and interprets the request.

variants.explanation: The browser talks to the service. The service decides what to query; the database returns data to the service, not directly to the browser.
variants.hint: Start with the component that needs information. A database cannot return a record before it receives a query.

variants.title: Trace the response
variants.context: A response carries a result back to the requester. The service turns stored data into the response the client expects.
variants.prompt: The database has found the saved destination. What happens next?

items.text: The browser follows the redirect to the saved destination.
The service sends a response to the browser.
The database returns the record to the service.

variants.explanation: Data returns to the service first. The service creates the response, and the browser interprets that response.
variants.hint: Follow the return journey: database → service → client.

variants.title: Survive a restart
variants.context: Durable storage retains data when an application process stops. A variable held only in service memory disappears when that process restarts.
variants.prompt: Your service stores a new short link only in a local variable, then restarts. What should change so the information survives?
options: Keep another variable in the same process.
Write the information to durable storage before confirming success.
optionFeedback: Both variables disappear with the same process. No durable copy was created.
The acknowledged write has a durable copy the restarted service can read.
Retrying does not recreate information that was never persisted.
variants.explanation: Important application data needs an acknowledged durable write. Restarting a process clears its in-memory variables.
variants.hint: Which option puts the information outside the process that can restart?
